seat.BEST_WHY: The paving is the only genuinely hand-built material in the deck. In the lit area around the figure (roughly x 310–620, y 380–570) the courses are staggered and the stones vary in length *within* a single course — a short stone of about 20px sits beside one of about 55px in the same run, and the run above breaks at a different point, so the bond reads as laid rather than tiled. Each stone carries its own bevel and its own wear: on the course just above the figure one slab has three short parallel scratches, its neighbour has a diagonal hatch, the next is clean. The joints hold a consistent 2px dark value across the whole field without ever merging two stones into one blob, which is what usually breaks at this size. Compare the same floor in 1, where joints fade in and out and stones dissolve into each other.
seat.WORST_WHY: There is no architecture in it. Gamma-lifted, the frame is a floor-plan rectangle — paving from about x 310 to 735, y 200 to 570, plus a small annex at x 118–310, y 320–455, plus a corridor strip x 515–585 running to the bottom edge — and every pixel outside that outline is one structureless grey-brown noise field that runs to all four edges. The room's south edge at y≈570 is a razor-straight 1px transition from slab to noise: no wall, no threshold, no thickness, no cast shadow. Worse, the crack decals are not masked to the floor. At the top left, a crack enters at x=0, y≈255 and runs right across bare noise where there is no masonry to crack, then meets the paving. Two masonry fragments float in the void with nothing attached — a two-course bar at x 88–215, y 262–285, and a longer one at x 285–730, y 135–160 — each terminating in mid-air at both ends. On top of that the slab surfaces are soft: the joints are 1–2px anti-aliased grey rather than a chosen value, and the diagonal hatch marks repeat at an identical 45° and identical spacing on stone after stone. At 1:1 it reads as a filter pass over a floor blit, which is precisely the thing the bar exists to catch.

flip_list: Mask the crack decal layer to the floor footprint. The crack entering at x=0, y≈255 crosses ~90px of void before reaching any stone; clip it at the floor edge.
Delete or attach the two floating masonry bars (x 88–215, y 262–285; x 285–730, y 135–160). A wall run that starts and ends in mid-air with no return and no thickness is worse than no wall.

Build an actual wall at the room perimeter. The south edge at y≈570 is a 1px material change; it needs a wall body of at least one tile with a top surface at a different value from the lit floor, a visible thickness, and a dark contact line where it meets the floor.

Replace the void fill. Right now the same structureless noise serves as bedrock, as out-of-bounds, and as whatever the corridor cuts through. Give it either a real material with structure, or take it to near-black and let the light falloff do the work.

Sharpen the joints to a chosen value at a chosen width instead of the current 1–2px anti-aliased grey that fades out toward the light edge. Stones in the bright centre currently merge into one another.
Vary the surface hatching. The 45° diagonal hatch appears at the same angle and same spacing on at least a dozen slabs across the frame; rotate, re-space, and remove it from most stones.
law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
